transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What has brought you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m losing a lot of time rechecking things. Like my dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes… I just don’t feel like I can move on until I’ve gone through the same routine enough times that the anxiety comes down. It’s starting to take up hours.
When you’re rechecking things like locks or your notes, do you feel at some level that the amount of checking you’re doing is excessive or unreasonable, or does it feel completely necessary to you?

I know it’s excessive, yeah. Like part of me can see I’ve already checked the lock or the file dimensions enough times. But in the moment it still feels like I’m not allowed to move on until I repeat the routine and the anxiety drops. That’s the part that’s taking hours.

Aside from the checking itself, do you get intrusive thoughts or mental images that pop into your mind against your will and feel distressing or senseless, which you then try to neutralize or relieve by checking?

Yes. It’s like even after I know I’ve cleaned the wound area, or I’ve already reviewed a CAD file, this thought cuts in that I missed one tiny thing. And then my mind goes to, like, what if that turns into an infection, or what if it’s a design mistake that hurts someone. I can tell it doesn’t really make sense at that point, but I can’t just reason it away, so I end up checking again.
On a typical day, roughly how much total time do you spend on these checking routines, from when they start until you can finally move on?

Usually it adds up to hours in a day. Not all in one block, but from starting the checks to finally feeling like I can move on, it can eat up a big part of the day. I’ll recheck things like the locks, dressing supplies, file dimensions, or notes until the anxiety comes down enough.
Because of all this checking, what in your life has actually been affected the most—like your work, studies, relationships, or daily routine?

Mostly work and my routine outside work. My project deadlines have started slipping because I’ll stay late trying to feel comfortable enough to submit something. And then I’m missing things I used to do for myself, like paddleboarding meetups or workouts, because the checking routines end up taking that time.

Outside of those specific checking situations, do you also tend to feel worried or tense about lots of different everyday things most of the day, even when you’re not in the middle of a checking routine?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think it’s about lots of different things most of the day. It feels more tied to those specific moments where I think I missed something, and then I get tense until I check. Outside of that, I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed constant general worry.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or noticeably sad most days, even when you’re not caught up in the checking?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated and worn out by the checking, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down or sad most days outside of that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent, intrusive doubts about having made small mistakes or missed details (e.g., wound cleaning, CAD files, locks) that are experienced as excessive and not fully reasonable, yet cannot be dismissed by logic. These obsessions drive repetitive checking rituals (locks, dressing supplies, file dimensions, revision notes) performed to reduce anxiety. The compulsions take up hours per day, cause significant functional impairment at work (missed deadlines) and in leisure activities (missing paddleboarding and workouts), and are ego-dystonic. There is no evidence of a pervasive generalized anxiety pattern or a primary mood disorder. This presentation is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
